summary: Remove the tally projection watermark and make rebuilds compare-and-set only (#124)
details: * fix(ballots): make the tally projection rebuild compare-and-set only The merged projection skipped increments whose vote timestamp was at or below an appliedThrough watermark that a rebuild believed it had counted. Under concurrency that watermark was wrong: a vote could be visible to the increment but not the recount, so the increment was skipped and the row under-counted. The full suite failed on main with 7 votes in the row against 8 votes. Remove appliedThrough and its timestamp guard entirely. Increments always apply: each is one atomic upsert of the choice, total and an internal monotonic version. Nothing is skipped. The rebuild is now absolute and compare-and-set only. It reads the row version (0 when the row is missing), recounts every bound vote, and writes absolute counts only if the version is unchanged, advancing it by one. A mismatch recounts and retries, bounded. A concurrent increment either lands before the recount (the absolute write is correct) or after the compare-and-set (it adds on top). The 500 ms deadline still writes nothing, leaving the row for the repair CLI. Revision moves remain transactional deltas and certification still never reads the projection. Tests: 20 rounds that deterministically interleave an increment between the rebuild's recount and its compare-and-set (and after it), asserting exact equality with the authoritative bound tally every round; an increment after an absolute rebuild is applied; the concurrent first-vote, change and revision-move cases remain. The projection test file raises its write deadline under load because a timed-out write is allowed to be abandoned; the timeout case still asserts that nothing is written. Refs #52 * docs(status): record the compare-and-set-only projection rebuild Removes the appliedThrough watermark description and records the merged under-count it caused. Documents the current contract: unconditional atomic increments, transactional revision moves, and an absolute recount that writes only when the row version is unchanged, retries when it moved, and writes nothing at its deadline. Records the 20-round interleaved race test, the 12-test projection suite run ten times, both 713-test full-suite runs, the residual delayed-increment window, and the configurable test deadline. Refs #52 * chore(changelog): record the compare-and-set-only tally projection Regenerates the public snapshot from this branch's history. The generator's fixed 80-commit window drops the oldest entries, which is the pre-existing truncation tracked in #96, not a decision in this slice. summary: Paginate the public list and add a display-only tally projection (#52) (#112)
details: * feat(ballots): project display-only tallies after a committed vote Public list pages (/ and /proposals/) tallied every vote and decrypted every encrypted ballot just to show a count. Add a display-only ballot_tallies row per (ballotId, revisionId), written best-effort after the vote transaction commits. The projection is never authoritative: recordFormalDecision keeps recomputing the outcome from the bound votes and does not read it. A failed or slow projection write is logged as an operational event and cannot fail, delay or alter the vote. Vote changes decrement the previous choice and increment the new one, a re-cast of the same choice is a no-op, and rows are revision-scoped. The row stores counts and a timestamp only: no member id, choice, reason or envelope. listProposals can now omit vote tallies so public reads never touch proposal_votes; the web pages overlay certified results and the projection in the next commit. Adds the unique compound index to initializeDatabase and a rebuild/repair path for the CLI. Refs #52 * perf(proposals): paginate the public list and stop scanning ballots /proposals/ loaded every proposal, applied search, stage, branch and sort in the page, and decrypted every vote for the row totals. It now reads a bounded display page of 25 rows from MongoDB with server-side pagination. - Page, total, page count and range are computed from the filtered set; invalid or out-of-range pages clamp; ties order deterministically by proposal id. - Links keep q, stage, branch, space, sort, focus and joined; changing a filter starts at page 1. Pagination uses the Button primitive with previous/next and a live range status. - Each page self-references its canonical address and emits rel=prev/rel=next. The repository has no noIndex convention for parameterised lists, so pages stay indexable with a self-canonical rather than inventing one. - Rows no longer read proposal_votes. A certified ballot shows the tally stored on ballot_results; otherwise a fresh ballot_tallies row is used; a missing or stale row shows "Voting open — tally updating" with a link to the matter. - / overlays the same projection on the register it already reads, so home no longer decrypts votes either. Matters without a trustworthy aggregate are left out of the highlights rather than showing a wrong percentage. Visibility is still decided by canViewProposal and re-checked after the coarse MongoDB pre-filter; eligibility, ballot binding and deadlines are untouched. Refs #52 * feat(scripts): rebuild the ballot tally projection from votes Add npm run ballots:tally-projection. It reports missing, mismatched and orphan projection rows against the votes they should represent, and with --apply rebuilds them. It never deletes, edits or rewrites a vote and never certifies a result. Dry run is the default; --verify exits non-zero when rows need repair; an explicit --database is required; production writes additionally require --allow-production and --confirm-production engage_production. Encrypted votes need the ballot keys and the tool refuses to write a partial tally without them. Refs #52 * fix(proposals): keep the active stage tab and certified tallies correct The parsed stage is now '' rather than 'all' for an unfiltered list, so the All tab has to compare against '' to stay marked current. A certified result is authoritative even when the matter no longer carries a ballotRevisionId (for example after a zero-vote unbind). Resolve certified results by every visible matter's ballot, not only those with a current binding, so the row shows the recorded tally instead of falling back to no tally. Refs #52 * docs(status): record public list pagination and the tally projection Adds the before/after harness snapshots for / and /proposals/ (before 57402f0, after 65ace21) and records what changed: 25-row server pagination with filter preservation and canonical/rel links, a display-only ballot_tallies projection, certified tallies from ballot_results, and a neutral tally-updating state for missing or stale rows. The profiler window records 3 -> 0 proposal_votes operations on /proposals/ and 6 -> 0 on /, with getMore batches falling from three to one on every measured public page. Reports the /proposals/ HTML increase honestly: it renders 25 rows instead of 15 at the specified page size, not extra markup per row. Updates I12 and S4, notes the detail page's remaining live tally and the deployment step to backfill the projection, and adds the new collection and CLI to the architecture docs. Refs #52 * fix(ballots): move a re-bound amendment tally to the right revision row An amendment ballot can be re-bound to a newer wording revision. A member who had already voted on the previous revision casts again on the new one, so the previous count belongs to the old row, not the new row. The projection now learns the revision the previous vote was bound to and recounts both rows from their votes instead of applying a delta to the wrong row. Main matter ballots cannot reach this path: castVote refuses a ballot whose existing votes are not all bound to its current revision. Adds a projection test for the move. Refs #52 * docs(status): correct the public-list suite count The final run includes the revision-move projection test: 655 tests, 0 fail. Refs #52 * chore(changelog): record public list pagination and the tally projection Regenerates the public snapshot from this branch's history. The generator's fixed 80-commit window drops the oldest entries, which is the pre-existing truncation tracked in #96, not a decision in this slice. Refs #52 * fix(ballots): make tally projection writes atomic under concurrency The projection's first-vote path read the votes and wrote absolute counts when no row existed. A concurrent increment could land between that read and write, or after it, double counting; the full suite exposed it as an extra abstain. The normal path is now one atomic upsert increment, so a first vote creates the row and counts it in a single operation. Two concurrent first votes can no longer each create a row or lose one. A write conflict from a transactional revision move retries inside the deadline. The only remaining recount is for an unreadable prior vote and the repair CLI. It is compare-and-set guarded on an internal version token and bounded by a watermark recorded in appliedThrough, so an increment for a vote the recount already included is skipped, and an increment that landed first forces a fresh recount. The deadline is enforced before each write (and with maxTimeMS on the recount), so a timed-out rebuild leaves the row for the repair CLI instead of writing a stale absolute count. A revision move is two transactional deltas on the old and new rows, not a recount. A row whose counts are negative or do not sum to its total is never displayed; it reads as tally pending until repaired. Tests: many concurrent first votes, concurrent vote changes and a concurrent revision move each equal the authoritative tally; ten rebuild-versus-increment races; a recorder that a timed-out rebuild writes nothing; and the public list treating an inconsistent row as pending. Refs #52 * docs(status): record the race-safe projection write strategy Replaces the read-then-write description with the atomic strategy: an upsert increment for normal votes, transactional deltas for a revision move, and a compare-and-set recount bounded by a watermark and deadline for the last-resort path. Records that an internally inconsistent row is displayed as pending, the residual out-of-order watermark caveat, the concurrency tests and both full suite results. Refs #52 * chore(changelog): record the race-safe tally projection writes Regenerates the public snapshot from this branch's history. The generator's fixed 80-commit window drops the oldest entries, which is the pre-existing truncation tracked in #96, not a decision in this slice. summary: Paginate the proposal register and stop reading ballots (#52) (#103)
details: * perf(admin): paginate the proposal register and stop reading ballots The proposals register loaded every proposal, including its rationale, and decrypted every vote for the rows in Decide so it could show live tallies. It sent ~1 MB of HTML and did per-vote work on a list read. The register now reads a bounded page of 25 rows from MongoDB, ordered by proposal id, with search, stage and branch filters applied server-side and the viewer's branch scope preserved. Page links keep the active filters; changing a filter starts at page 1; invalid or out-of-range pages clamp. Pagination uses the existing Button primitive with previous/next, the current page and a status region announcing the visible range. `listProposalRegister` projects the register fields only (no `details` or `detailHtml`) and never touches `proposal_votes`, so no ballot is decrypted on a list read. For a certified ballot it shows the tally, computed result and rule basis stored on `ballot_results` at certification. An open ballot shows "Open — view ballot" instead of live counts, and a closed but uncertified ballot links to the workspace to record the outcome. The detail workspace keeps the live bound tally and the result form unchanged; recording from the list would require decrypting every vote. Editing, revising and creating still resolve their full record, including rationale, from any page, with the same scope and lock checks. Measured with `npm run perf:render` (78 synthetic proposals, 1200 votes, 3 runs, administrator): HTML 938,422 B → 283,915 B (−69.7%); document DB commands 19 → 16; document DB time 28.7 ms → 16.0 ms; TTFB 103.1 ms → 57.6 ms. The register's narrow projection only asked for the current field names, so the shared normaliser would have seen an empty identifier and defaulted the stage to Deliberate. Project the alias fields too (still excluding rationale and ballot data), and match the stage filter against a stored `status` when a document has no `stage`. Adds a regression case for a legacy-shaped record: it keeps its identifier, its normalised stage, its space, and remains searchable by rationale without returning it. summary: Validate recorded outcomes against the bound tally (#28) (#86)
details: * feat(ballots): validate recorded outcomes against the bound tally Record a formal ballot outcome only after comparing the officer's result with the outcome computed from the votes bound to that ballot and immutable revision (#28). The comparison is deliberately limited to what the decision register settles: Yes greater than No approves and a tie does not (D9); abstentions are recorded and excluded rather than given a denominator (D10, O1); no quorum, turnout or minimum-participation threshold applies (D8). The basis is versioned as `simple-majority-d9-v1`. A contradicting result is refused unless the officer supplies a written reason, and is then stored as an explicit override. The result keeps the tally at certification, the rule basis and the computed result; the `decision.recorded` event records the actor, reason, computed result and recorded result alongside the existing atomic result and ballot certification. Identical retries remain idempotent, conflicting replacements are refused, and historical results are returned unchanged and never rewritten. Both admin result forms now show the computed outcome and its tally before submission and require the override reason when the chosen result contradicts it, using the shared Field, Textarea and Badge primitives. * test(ballots): cover computed outcomes, overrides and stored evidence Add rule-level cases for approval, rejection, a tie, zero votes and abstention-heavy ballots, plus the two admin form behaviours that reveal and require an override reason. Add real-MongoDB replica-set coverage for the parts that prove persistence and the ordered result write: the tally and rule basis stored on the result, rejection of a contradiction without a reason, an audited override, idempotent retries, refused replacement, encrypted-ballot certification through the decryption path, and a historical result that stays readable and unrewritten. The result API is exercised end to end with the dev session. Refs #28. * docs(governance): record computed ballot outcome validation Describe the computed Yes-versus-No check, its `simple-majority-d9-v1` basis, the stored tally and the audited override in the lifecycle, API and agent guides. Mark known gap 10 as partly resolved and keep #28/L1 Partial because the abstention denominator (O1), quorum and ranked choice remain undecided. * chore(changelog): regenerate the public changelog snapshot * feat(ballots): certify only a closed ballot from a consistent bound tally Refuse certification while a ballot can still accept votes. A result is accepted when the ballot has a closure marker, its close time has passed, or the system has already closed it; a live ballot returns BALLOT_NOT_CLOSED and a ballot with no recorded close is refused rather than assumed closed, because a later vote could contradict an early certification. The tally query reads only the fields the check needs. Reject an override reason longer than 1000 characters instead of truncating audit evidence, and treat a retry that changes the recorded override reason as a conflict rather than an idempotent success. The refusal message now names the computed outcome and says that any other result, including inconclusive, requires a written reason. Refs #28. * feat(admin): show the enforced tally and recorded outcomes Derive the admin outcome basis from the same bound tally that certification enforces, so a page can no longer show a tally the server will not count. A zero-vote ballot reads "No votes yet — outcome not yet computable" instead of "Unsuccessful", and an unbound or unreadable tally is named instead of guessed.
